issues.failure_explanation: In Proposition 4.1, the truncation half-width is set to $b = \sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2} \ln N}$. The total integration error $|I(f) - Q_N(f)|$ includes the domain truncation error $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d \setminus [-b,b]^d} f(\boldsymbol{x}) \rho(\boldsymbol{x}) \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{x}$. For the constant function $f = 1 \in H_\rho^\alpha(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the Gaussian tail error satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d \setminus [-b,b]^d} \rho(\boldsymbol{x}) \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{x} \gtrsim \frac{e^{-b^2/2}}{b} = \frac{N^{-\alpha/4}}{\sqrt{(\alpha/2)\ln N}}$. Since $N^{-\alpha/4}$ decays strictly slower than the claimed upper bound rate $O(N^{-\alpha} (\ln N)^\gamma)$ for every $\alpha \ge 1$, the stated error bound fails for the chosen $b$.

failure_location.quote: let $Q_{N}$ be the rank-$1$ lattice rule defined in \eqref{eq:affine-QMC} with $b=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2}\ln N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase the truncation parameter to $b = 2\sqrt{\alpha \ln N}$ (or any $b \ge \sqrt{2\alpha \ln N}$, analogous to Proposition 4.2), so that $e^{-b^2/2} \le N^{-\alpha}$ and the truncation error is bounded by $O(N^{-\alpha})$.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate guarantee of $O(N^{-\alpha} (\ln N)^{\frac{3\alpha d}{2} + \frac{d}{4}})$ in Proposition 4.1 and its corresponding entry in Theorem 4.10 fail as stated for $b = \sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2} \ln N}$, because the actual error is bounded below by $\Omega(N^{-\alpha/4} (\ln N)^{-1/2})$.
issues.title: Insufficient domain truncation parameter in affinely-mapped lattice rule
issues.why_classification: A routine local adjustment of the scaling parameter $b$ from $\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2} \ln N}$ to $2\sqrt{\alpha \ln N}$ restores the validity of the proof and preserves the optimal rate $N^{-\alpha}$, the logarithmic exponent, and all guarantees without requiring new proof architecture.
